titolo: Trump: Iran War Ends 'Whenever I Want' — Then Two Italians Die
angolo: Trump's boast of control over the war's end collides with a deadly Kuwait attack Iran says it didn't carry out, and a mystery over who launched the drone.
descrizione: Trump: Iran War Ends 'Whenever I Want' — Then Two Italians Die. On Thanksgiving, President Trump told troops victory is 'at hand' and named Pickaxe Mountain as a target. Hours earlier, two Italian technicians were killed in Kuwait; Kuwait and Italy blame Iran, Tehran denies it. Here is what is confirmed, what is disputed, and what comes next.

scene.testo: Two Italian technicians were working in Kuwait. They never came home.
They were working at an air-defence surveillance station when drones targeted Kuwaiti military sites, according to Italy's foreign minister.
Hours later, Trump told troops on a Thanksgiving call: we have victory at hand.
His words: it's going to be, sort of, whenever I want it to be.

citazione.testo: It's going to be whenever, sort of, whenever I want it to be, to be honest.

scene.testo: But who launched the drone that killed the two Italians? Italy and Kuwait blame Iran. Iran denies it.

grafica.sotto: Trump says he controls the end. Iran denies the attack.

scene.testo: Can one man really end a war that others keep feeding?
Stay with me. Iran's denial comes with a twist.
First, the afternoon in Kuwait.
Around two in the afternoon local time, a drone strike hit a Kuwaiti military installation, Tajani told the Italian Senate, according to UPI.
Kuwait's army says it detected and engaged the drones.
Kuwait says a 'vital site' was targeted in what it called an Iranian attack.
Four people were wounded at first by falling debris, Kuwait's defense ministry reported.
Two of them were Italians. They later died of their injuries.
The other two wounded were a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national.
They worked for Rheinmetall Italia, the Italian unit of German defense group Rheinmetall, Tajani said.
Italy's foreign ministry says they were maintaining detection antennas for Kuwait's air defense.
Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told the Senate what Rome believes happened.
Drones of Iranian origin, he said, targeted Kuwaiti military installations, including the station.

citazione.testo: Several drones of Iranian origin targeted Kuwaiti military installations.

scene.testo: Tajani later told reporters the drone used in the attack was manufactured in Iran. Tehran has not accepted that account.
But there is a detail many headlines skip.
Al Jazeera reports the men died from falling debris, as authorities tried to intercept Iranian drones.
Kuwait's defense ministry said four people were wounded by debris as forces dealt with the drones.
Al Jazeera's correspondent also reported an Italian delegation was visiting Kuwait at the time.
Among them, Al Jazeera's reporter said, was the commander general of the Carabinieri, Lt. Gen. Salvatore Lungo.
Now, Tehran's answer.
Iran's armed forces spokesman Abolfazl Shekarchi said no military or offensive operations had been conducted in the region.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi wrote on X that the incident was suspicious.

citazione.testo: The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war.

scene.testo: He offered to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to find the cause.
An Iranian armed forces spokesman called it a false-flag operation, without providing evidence.
Araghchi also called his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts to offer condolences.
Per Tajani, Araghchi rejected claims the drone was launched by Iranian forces or from Iranian territory.
So we have two accounts that cannot both be true.
Kuwait and Italy blame Iran. Iran denies it. We have not seen an independent finding made public.

grafica.sotto: No independent finding has been published

scene.testo: Kuwait's defense ministry condemned what it called 'heinous Iranian aggression'.
Giorgia Meloni expressed her deepest sympathy and offered her heartfelt condolences to the victims' families.
Israel's foreign minister, Gideon Sa'ar, used the moment to criticize Iran.
Why does this attack matter beyond the tragedy?
Just over a week ago, Kuwait said it repelled Iranian drone attacks on an airbase hosting US forces, the first strikes in more than two months, the BBC reported.
The same day, ABC reported attacks on two ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
The war began on February 28 with joint US and Israeli strikes.
Tehran closed the Strait of Hormuz. Washington blockaded Iran's ports.
Last week, Iran said three tankers hit mines despite US escort.
Washington widened sanctions on more than two dozen Iranian entities.
Now back to the man who says he holds the clock.
Donald Trump spoke from Mar-a-Lago on Thanksgiving Day.
He was calling troops deployed overseas from Mar-a-Lago, alongside Melania Trump.
'And we have victory at hand,' he told them.
He said the US was giving Iran every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives.
But he added he is not sure Tehran will take it.
Then the military message: 'We sent an extra aircraft carrier there. We're loaded up.'

citazione.testo: We sent an extra aircraft carrier there. We're loaded up.

scene.testo: Remember: a third carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, arrived in the Middle East on November 15, US officials said.
It joined the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington.
Trump did not say which carrier he meant. Reports do not specify.
Then he named a target.
Pickaxe Mountain.
It is a heavily fortified underground facility near Iran's Natanz uranium enrichment complex, Iran International reports.
Trump said the US would 'absolutely hit Pickaxe Mountain' if it takes further action.

citazione.testo: We would absolutely hit Pickaxe Mountain.

scene.testo: Yet he also said, 'we haven't seen any real activity there.'
He said he spoke with Netanyahu in recent days, per Iran International.
He also claimed Iran's military is 'decimated', in his words.
And that China and Russia, he said, are 'helping me' on an Iran deal.
'We can put that war to bed anytime we want,' he said.
So why say it now? Look at the clock in Washington.
The war is in its ninth month.
The Pentagon estimates the war has cost $48.3 billion, according to The Hill.
Trump told the New York Post that operations against Iran are funded through the end of January.
Trump said he finds it hard to believe Democrats would turn a win into a loss.
And the open question: who launched that drone over Kuwait?
Iran offers a joint probe. Kuwait and Italy blame Tehran.
Whatever the answer, two Italian families are in mourning.
One president says the war will end whenever he wants it to.
